name: Calorite-F
description: Calorite-F is a CNT aerogel foam produced by Tessera Materials through supercritical drying of a multi-walled CNT hydrogel, yielding an open-cell foam structure with thermal conductivity below 0.012 W/m·K — lower than still air — while retaining enough structural integrity to absorb significant compressive impact loads before permanent deformation. The material is 97% air by volume, giving it a density of approximately 8 kg/m³, and its CNT skeleton provides modest electrical conductivity that can be tuned during manufacture. Calorite-F is used wherever extreme thermal insulation and impact damping must coexist in a low-mass package: cryogenic vessel liners, re-entry vehicle heat shields, sensitive equipment shipping, and high-end protective casings.
applications: re-entry vehicle and hypersonic heat shielding
sensitive electronics and augment component shipping cases
thermal management layers in powered armor
acoustic dampening panels in secure facilities
cost: Φ190 per kg (standard grade); Φ740 per kg (high-temp re-entry grade)
story_hooks: A sealed Calorite-F shipping case arrives at a Shelf drop-point addressed to no one — the thermal signature inside reads as a living body at cryo-preservation temperatures. Someone paid to have a person shipped, and the payment trail has been scrubbed clean.

Calorite-F panels are standard in secure server room insulation — but a runner discovers that a particular batch installed in a corporate data center has had its electrical conductivity tuned to passively harvest and re-radiate EM emissions from the servers inside, feeding a receiver in the building's ventilation stack.

A black-market supplier is selling Calorite-F at deep discount to Shelf residents for habitat insulation — it works perfectly, but the foam was sourced from demolished military installations and carries trace contamination that the seller is aware of and the buyers are not.
